questions.question: Does executable evidence establish: Unknown clients cannot obtain codes or tokens from stored Google credentials; owner identity and explicit client consent are mandatory.
Does executable evidence establish: Browser callbacks enforce session-bound single-use state, nonce, expiry, owner and transition checks; logout/revocation interleavings never restore access.
Does executable evidence establish: OAuth enforces PKCE, redirect/client/resource binding, tasks scope, refresh rotation and grant revocation with no cross-client mutation.
Does executable evidence establish: Versioned private atomic storage fails closed, locks out concurrent processes, migrates disconnected and rejects legacy MCP sessions.
Does executable evidence establish: Trusted stop-first owner setup and CLI administration work without network ownership enrollment; hosted and local configuration validate securely.
Are failures redacted and changes limited to the reviewed authentication scope?
Does one auth module own each invariant with typed transitions and no duplicated policy?
Do real HTTP and stateful interleavings distinguish owner approval from stored credentials?
Are wrong-owner, replay, resource, scope and cross-client boundaries enforced by production code?
Are atomic persistence, lifecycle limits and deployment defaults explicit and tested?
Does evidence cover every frozen checklist and generated applicable ordering in acceptance-criteria.md, with real production composition and no live path inferred from mocked tests?
